title: Nearly half of Arkansas is in exceptional drought
lede: Exceptional drought (D4) is the worst of the Drought Monitor's five drought levels.
We show how much of each state's land was at that level on four maps.

big.label: of Arkansas in exceptional drought (D4), map valid Nov 10, 2026

chart.title: Share of each state's land in drought, four Drought Monitor maps
series: Extreme drought or worse (D3 or D4)

facts.text: 49.5% of Arkansas was in exceptional drought (D4) on the Nov 10 map, up from 39.7% a week earlier.
facts.source: U.S. Drought Monitor (National Drought Mitigation Center, USDA, NOAA), map valid Nov 10, 2026

facts.text: It was 6.6% four weeks earlier (Oct 13) and 0% a year earlier (Nov 11, 2025).
facts.source: U.S. Drought Monitor (National Drought Mitigation Center, USDA, NOAA), map valid Nov 10, 2026

facts.text: 84.6% of Arkansas was in extreme drought or worse (D3 or D4), up from 82.1% a week earlier.
facts.source: U.S. Drought Monitor (National Drought Mitigation Center, USDA, NOAA), map valid Nov 10, 2026

facts.text: 57 of Arkansas's 75 counties had some exceptional drought, up from 48 a week earlier and 20 four weeks earlier.
facts.source: U.S. Drought Monitor (National Drought Mitigation Center, USDA, NOAA), map valid Nov 10, 2026

facts.text: In 37 of those counties, at least half the land was in exceptional drought.
facts.source: U.S. Drought Monitor (National Drought Mitigation Center, USDA, NOAA), map valid Nov 10, 2026

facts.text: Louisiana: 18.9% in exceptional drought, 58.6% in D3 or worse. Mississippi: 7.5% in exceptional drought, 46.5% in D3 or worse.
facts.source: U.S. Drought Monitor (National Drought Mitigation Center, USDA, NOAA), map valid Nov 10, 2026
